scope: Allocation-lifetime byte admission for PreparedReply and PreparedCancellation revocation-work vectors, plus inert complete-parent ownership of active returned-memory preparations, detached storage and pending notifications. Existing original-token sponsorship and consuming physical cleanup remain local to each typed parent.
artifact_note: All eight final changed/new Rust sources were frozen before native campaigns and checked against the retained source identities. Later documentation changes and an existing unrelated manual PDF edit affect per-run tracked-diff captures; the PDF is excluded from this change. Source, kernel, boot-image, disk, manifest, serial and selected service hashes identify exercised artifacts. Relevant diagnostics are included inline. Existing signed version-10 service bundles were reused; each runner regenerated signed security fixtures.

policy.charge: [allocated requested layout bytes, 0 node slots], before Global allocation; actual deallocation precedes original-class refund
policy.maximum_note: Layout-derived bound; the new real mapped-loan lifecycle controls use two work entries, not 255 simultaneous physical loans.
policy.layout_note: These are inline stack parents, with no new holder allocation. Capability/endpoint/pending/reply payload-node layouts and queue slot layouts do not change.
policy.class: Clone the accepted token loan-vector allocator during identity capture, before root leasing/revalidation. Ordinary-token promotion and a different reply/closing actor cannot select trusted backing or redirect refunds. Allocator clones themselves reserve nothing.
policy.decision: Keep numerical defaults. One maximum work array requests about 49.8 KiB within the existing 12/16 MiB pool; vectors contribute zero node slots and reuse the same accounting and administration. Full mixed-workload pressure is not qualified. Raising limits adds retained-heap headroom and may reduce denials, but cannot guarantee saturated cleanup progress. A hard guarantee would require earlier cleanup-capacity reservation and integrated pressure acceptance.
policy.cleanup_admission: Capacity is requested at reply/cancellation preparation, not reserved when the call is accepted. Saturation can return ResourceLimit before claim and postpone cleanup/root retirement while accepted authority/backing remain intact. Empty work needs no allocation or byte headroom.
policy.abi: 23-pool catalog, statistics version 10, SDK/runtime wire formats and logical resource limits unchanged; no service source or bundle rebuild required

ownership.parent: PreparedReply and PreparedCancellation wrap one complete resource struct in ManuallyDrop. Work capacity, exact leases or borrowed closing owner, claims, active returned-memory transfer, hidden grants, retired records/attachments and pending notifications have no implicit destruction on parent abandonment.
ownership.preparation: Prepare full work capacity before LoanRevocation receipts or token claim publication. Quota denial leaves the accepted token/call unclaimed; allocated unstarted prefixes cancel only their actual typed receipts. Ordinary preparation errors explicitly finish returned preparations and buffer storage after local IPC guards, before root completion.
ownership.finish: Pop consumes each typed child outside IPC; empty length retains full vector capacity and original class. Success or known-unstarted rollback disposes metadata/attachments, frees the empty work allocation before roots, then dispatches pending notifications. Physical failure keeps the consumed child's existing terminal fence/pin and backing charges; empty parent-buffer disposal is no physical completion/replay proof.
ownership.returned_memory: Abandonment now retains the actual returned-memory transfer, source escrow/pin and unpublished destination instead of running its active destructor. Nonwaiting source close stays busy and hidden destinations remain unavailable. Explicit ordinary unstarted-error cleanup still restores source ownership.
ownership.fallback: Guarded Drop is terminal retention, not a recoverable transaction or permission to reconstruct an owner from IDs, counters or backing. No cleanup registry or new owner-family row is introduced.

validation.host_suite: Complete scripts/run-host-tests.sh passed with local socket access, including expected rejecting parser/backend controls. Existing production ByteAllocator tests trace actual deallocation-before-refund, complete old/candidate overlap, backend-error rollback and immutable allocator class; no host physical-loan model is substituted for native completion.
validation.native_builds: All runners built final kernels and enforced executable/read-only assembly section checks.
native_controls: Reply and queued/delivered cancellation use actual mapped loans. Explicit counter-pressure reservations leave one byte less than the full two-entry work candidate. Preparation rejects under the heap guard before claim, with unchanged epoch, accepted borrows, mappings and counters. Ordinary callers are promoted after call acceptance; both ordinary and trusted original classes are exercised.

After pressure release, real work arrays have exact two-entry capacity and original allocator class. Counter snapshots remain fully charged through each consuming child and the final-pop reply publication callback. Queued ordinary cancellation additionally checks exact retained work bytes during both real move/copy attachment-release callbacks, after token/pending/cap disposal. Fixture close recovers exact original IPC counters.

Real zero-loan scalar tokens prepare work under a held heap guard at the ordinary byte ceiling, with zero capacity and unchanged usage; finish invokes no revocation callback and returns all original counters.

Existing partial physical-failure controls now assert exact work-buffer byte recovery after remaining unstarted children cancel; uncertain loan backing and token/root fences remain and no terminal result is published.

Actual complete reply and standalone cancellation parents are first dropped unguarded, then under lifecycle/table/IPC/heap/physical/memory-registry/capability-registry/pool guards after caller promotion. Exact work/node/authority/frame counters are unchanged. Reply keeps returned-memory escrow/pin and hidden grants; nonwaiting source close is busy. Cancellation keeps queue/claim/mapped loan. Both exact roots stay retained.

Actual endpoint-borrowing and namespace-borrowing cancellation parents are also dropped under the same guard set, retaining work capacity and original closing-owner/peer/root claims. Existing staged-close, closing-peers, claim-epoch, source-close, mapping, returned-output and producer-LP notification controls remain enabled.
validation.formatting: cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed.

remaining_limits: Cleanup work capacity is not pre-reserved at call acceptance. Saturation can reject or postpone reply/cancellation/root retirement while accepted authority remains retained. A numerical increase alone cannot establish hostile-pressure fairness or saturated teardown progress.
Other control storage, default image/package/store snapshot callers, allocator bookkeeping and general heap/aggregate principal admission remain open; SEC-07/18 remain partial.

Guarded probes cover actual claimed parents and borrowed endpoint/namespace variants. They do not independently force every physical-cleanup interruption/notification-dispatch phase or qualify every enclosing caller/IRQ/implicit-destructor context. Ordinary finishing still requires the existing qualified context; allocation/preparation under IPC and bounded-copy/guard latency remain separate work.

Backend allocation failure uses the existing shared allocator host adapter. Native general heap OOM and panic/unwind are not forced; quota controls use explicit counter reservations. Layout-derived maximum capacity is not a 255-loan physical-pressure campaign.

Terminal fixtures deliberately retain resources: two reply-abandonment fixtures keep two data pages each plus exact roots, returned-memory escrow/hidden grants and work bytes; two standalone cancellation-abandonment fixtures keep one data page each plus queue/claim/roots and work bytes. Existing failed/endpoint/namespace fixtures retain their original backings and now their work capacities too. None supplies a recovery or replay owner.
